findings.text: Each table entry pairs a human readable label with a filter program, a mode tag, a sample packet image, and a small list of expected outcomes. The program lives in a union offering fields named insns and insns_int, holding either a classic instruction sequence or an internal instruction sequence, selected by mode tags named CLASSIC and INTERNAL. Expected outcomes map truncated input extents to required return values, exercising empty, short, and full inputs from one shared packet image.

Classic programs combine absolute, indirect, and immediate loads with stores, arithmetic, miscellaneous register moves, conditional jumps, and returns. Absolute and indirect loads address packet bytes through link and network offset bases, while index seeding may use packet length or immediates. Arithmetic folds the index or an immediate into the accumulator, moves named TAX and TXA exchange accumulator and index, spills and fills named ST, STX, LD MEM, and LDX MEM preserve values across steps, and jumps test equality, ordered comparison, and bit presence before returning accumulator or immediate content.

Ancillary attribute loads add a shared base named SKF_AD_OFF to a field selector to read socket and device metadata rather than packet bytes. Selectors for packet type, mark, receive hash, queue mapping, protocol, virtual LAN tag and presence are named SKF_AD_PKTTYPE, SKF_AD_MARK, SKF_AD_RXHASH, SKF_AD_QUEUE, SKF_AD_PROTOCOL, SKF_AD_VLAN_TAG, and SKF_AD_VLAN_TAG_PRESENT. Further selectors for interface index, hardware type, processor identity, netlink and nested netlink lookup, payload offset discovery, and exclusive-or combination are named SKF_AD_IFINDEX, SKF_AD_HATYPE, SKF_AD_CPU, SKF_AD_NLATTR, SKF_AD_NLATTR_NEST, SKF_AD_PAY_OFFSET, and SKF_AD_ALU_XOR_X. Repeated identical loads check stability, while paired loads before and after packet byte checks confirm metadata survives interleaved packet access.

Internal programs exercise wide and narrow arithmetic over ten general registers with a dedicated return register. Operations include move, add, subtract, multiply, and shifts, in both immediate and register source forms, with explicit width selection between full register width and half register width. Control flow uses compare-and-skip branches on equality followed by an exit operation that delivers the return register as the program result, with chained arithmetic across all registers checking encoding and carry behavior uniformly.

The classic execution model implied by the vectors holds accumulator and index registers, a packet image with a truncation length, scratch memory slots, and a position within the program. Both registers start cleared, length loads publish the current truncation extent into the index, memory operations spill accumulator or index and reload them later, and register moves copy between accumulator and index. Conditional jumps skip forward on equality, ordered comparison, or bit presence, while terminal returns deliver either accumulator content or an immediate constant, with short inputs forcing defined fallback results instead of faults.

Each vector declares several truncated lengths with required return values, so one packet image validates empty, partial, and complete views. Short views that exclude referenced bytes expect zero or another defined fallback, boundary lengths flip decisions, and full views expect computed values such as sums, masked fields, or metadata echoes. Cases with repeated identical expectations across different truncation extents assert insensitivity to surplus bytes, while graded expectations assert monotonic or stepwise response to growing input.

Packet addressing and metadata tags treated as stable ABI include bases named SKF_LL_OFF, SKF_NET_OFF, and SKF_AD_OFF, plus socket echoes named SKB_TYPE, SKB_MARK, SKB_HASH, SKB_QUEUE_MAP, and SKB_VLAN_TCI. Additional echoes named SKB_VLAN_PRESENT, SKB_DEV_IFINDEX, and SKB_DEV_TYPE cover tag presence and device identity, with the Internet ethertype named ETH_P_IP and a maximal return constant named MAX_K. The fragment pairs each load selector with its expected echo constant, establishing that metadata loads must return those host-provided values unchanged when the synthetic packet is absent or short.

Loads that reference bytes outside the current truncation extent, including link, network, transport, and nested attribute traversals, must complete without fault and yield defined fallbacks. Vectors probe this by pairing tiny truncations that hide headers with larger truncations that reveal them, by walking nested attributes beyond available bytes, and by discovering payload offsets from short Ethernet plus Internet images. Ancillary metadata loads must similarly succeed on empty packets, returning host echoes rather than depending on packet content.

Netlink attribute vectors provide alternate byte images selected by a conditional named __BIG_ENDIAN, showing that attribute length and type fields swap order between big and little endian builds while expectations stay equivalent. Realistic capture vectors embed Ethernet plus Internet plus transport headers and exercise ethertype dispatch, protocol checks, fragment-bit masking, header-length scaling for indirect loads, and port matching with payload-length arithmetic using scratch slots. Spare operands on register moves reflect assembler tolerance for tool-emitted immediates that the interpreter must ignore.
